採用・広告の製品.quote: Alitheon — FeaturePrint® Optical-AI Object Authentication
FeaturePrint® Optical-AI Technology

FeaturePrint uses machine vision to identify, verify, and trace physical items from their inherent surface features. No labels, no barcodes, no tags, no chips — just a photo from a standard camera, even a mobile phone.
FeaturePrint® identifying and authenticating physical items from a single photograph.

Across every industry, organizations rely on barcodes, tags, labels, and etchings to identify and serialize physical items. These proxies can be damaged, removed, transferred, or counterfeited. When the wrong item enters your supply chain — either by mistake or through fraudulent activity — the consequences can be severe, ranging from financial loss to health & safety hazards.
FeaturePrint leverages the inherent micro-variations in every manufactured object — like a fingerprint for physical items. No modification. No special equipment. No training data.
Our optical-AI analyzes the object’s unique surface micro-features and creates a compact digital fingerprint — no larger than 500KB. No Training Data needed. Object agnostic.
At any point in the value chain, take another photo. FeaturePrint matches it with >99.9% accuracy and zero false positives.
No training data needed — works on any object, out of the box.
Why FeaturePrint Is Better
No training data needed
Anti-Counterfeit & Brand Protection

Authenticate the specific item — not just its class. FeaturePrint irrefutably verifies that the product in hand is the exact product that was manufactured, eliminating counterfeits, grey-market diversion, and fraudulent substitution at the individual item level. Full traceability and provenance from origin to end user. Think of it as Zero Trust for Things.
FeaturePrint operates in high-consequence environments where misidentification or fraud can result in financial loss, reputational damage, and health & safety risks.
Luxury Goods, Collectibles & Precious Metals
Protect brand integrity, verify provenance, and eliminate counterfeiting in high-value consumer markets.
Streamline inventory management and prevent fraudulent parts from entering sensitive government and military systems.
From circuit boards to server hardware, FeaturePrint serializes and authenticates electronic components without labels or markings.
FeaturePrint provides the certainty these environments demand: a tamper-proof, inherent digital identity that cannot be faked, removed, or transferred.
Tamper-proof by design
Built on a foundation that protects you too.

FeaturePrint is backed by a robust patent portfolio spanning 55+ issued patents across optical-AI identification, authentication, and traceability. When you deploy FeaturePrint, you are not just adopting a technology — you are building on an IP-protected foundation that shields your operations, your partnerships, and your competitive position.
Deep IP coverage across optical-AI identification, item authentication, serialization, and supply chain traceability — protecting the core technology that underpins your deployment.
Protection from Imitation
Partners and customers deploying FeaturePrint operate under the umbrella of Alitheon’s IP. Third parties cannot legally replicate the approach, safeguarding your competitive advantage.

1 / 7 · Healthcare & Personal Care · Product diversion

A global skincare brand was losing control of its authorized distribution. Genuine product intended for one channel was appearing at unauthorized sellers, and because the goods were real, no authenticity test flagged them. FeaturePrint gave each unit an identity taken from its own surface, so the brand could establish which specific units had left the authorized path and where they left it.
Individual units identified at unauthorized sellers, not just the production lots they came from
No change to the product, its packaging or the production line

The brand suspected it had a diversion problem and could not prove where it started. Genuine product was surfacing through sellers it had never authorized, at prices that undercut the partners who played by the rules.
The brand had batch and lot coding, as most manufacturers do. That identifies a production run, not a unit.
Channel information printed on outer packaging is removed or discarded before resale.

Each unit was enrolled at manufacture from a photograph of its own surface, and that identity was recorded against its authorized destination and channel. Nothing was added to the product or the packaging.

The identity a diverter would need to remove is the product's own surface. There is nothing to peel off, reprint or discard, so the link between a unit and its intended destination survives everything that happens to the packaging.
The same enrolled identity that exposed the diversion also authenticates the product at retail and in the secondary market, using the same photograph and the same workflow.
FeaturePrint for Healthcare
How a Distributor Caught Expired Product Relabeled With Extended Dates

Product that had passed its expiry date was being relabeled with extended dates and sold on. Every printed control on the package agreed with the fraud, because the fraud was the printing. FeaturePrint identified each unit from its own surface, which still matched the original enrollment and its true production record — regardless of what the new label said.
Relabeled units traced back to their original enrollment and true production record
Detection independent of anything printed on the package
Expired stock was re-entering the market with fresh labels showing later dates. To anyone inspecting the package, the product was in date. The label said so, and the label was new and clean.

This is a harder problem than counterfeiting. The product inside is the real product, made by the real manufacturer. Only one fact about it has been falsified, and that fact lives entirely on a printed surface that has been replaced.
Why printed controls could not catch it
Every conventional control for expiry is printed, which means relabeling defeats all of them at once.
The expiry date is printed, so a new label carries a new date.
Barcodes and serials are printed, so they are reprinted along with it.
Tamper-evident features protect the contents, not the accuracy of the date on the outside.
